The annual star-studded ceremony will honor movies released in theaters within the 2025 calendar year of eligibility. AMPAS members will vote on the Oscar winners in 24 categories, including Best Supporting Actress. But who will win? Here at Gold Derby, thousands of users have been making and updating their 2026 Oscar predictions for Best Supporting Actress, so let's take a look at all of the top contenders in our photo gallery below (updated March 4, 2026). These five Best Supporting Actress nominees are listed in order of their Gold Derby odds, which are derived from the combined forecasts of three unique groups: experts we’ve polled from major media outlets, editors who cover awards year-round for this website, and the top 24 users who had the best accuracy scores last year. The five most recent Best Supporting Actress champions at the Oscars are Zoe Saldaña for Emilia Pérez (2024) Da'Vine Joy Randolph for The Holdovers (2023), Jamie Lee Curtis for Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022), Ariana DeBose for West Side Story (2021), and Yuh-jung Youn for Minari (2020). Ready for some fun facts about past Best Supporting Actress Oscar nominees and winners? Shelley Winters (The Diary of Anne Frank and A Patch of Blue) and Dianne Wiest (Hannah and Her Sisters and Bullets Over Broadway) are tied with the most overall wins in this race at two apiece. Thelma Ritter has the most bids in this category at six, though she never won. The oldest winner is Peggy Ashcroft at 77 years old for A Passage to India (1984), while the youngest is Tatum O'Neal at 10 years old for Paper Moon (1973).
